value: Analysis of >6,500 metagenomes across 36 datasets from 6 continents and 25 countries
Reconstruction of >1,000 P. copri genomes (1,023 total: 17 isolates, 1,006 MAGs)
Four clades identified with >10% inter-clade genetic divergence
P. copri prevalence 95.4% in non-Westernized populations vs 29.6% in Westernized populations
61.6% of non-Westernized individuals harbor all four clades
Analysis of ancient metagenomes including Iceman (5,300-year-old) and pre-Columbian Mexican coprolites
Clade divergence estimated to pre-date human migration out of Africa (~90-194 ka)

extraction_warnings: The paper does not provide individual-level sample data with participant identifiers, sample IDs, or per-sample measurements. Instead, it reports aggregated population-level statistics (e.g., prevalence percentages, clade abundances, and genome counts) from >6,500 metagenomes across 36 datasets and multiple cohorts.

The paper describes four non-Westernized cohorts newly sequenced (Ghana: 44 individuals, Ethiopia: 50 individuals, Tanzania: 68 individuals, Madagascar: 110 individuals), but does not provide sample-level metadata or accessions for individual samples in the main text or supplementary tables reviewed.
Metadata such as age (with ranges and standard deviations), sex, and family relationships are reported at the cohort level but not mapped to individual samples.
While the paper references Tables S1, S2, S4, and S5 for metadata, the actual table contents are not included in the provided document, preventing extraction of per-sample data.
Ancient samples (Iceman and Mexican coprolites) are mentioned, but only 4 archaeological specimens are analyzed; they are not contemporary participants and represent different research objectives.

The granularity of this study is study_level and subgroup_level (by cohort, dataset, clade, disease phenotype, and westernization status), not sample_level. Setting granularity to sample_level and returning one generic not_reported entry to signal the absence of extractable per-sample rows.
Batch 1 returned granularity='study_level', differs from batch 0 ('sample_level'); kept batch 0.

This paper is a population genomics and metagenomics study of Prevotella copri across diverse human populations. The schema fields focus on clinical/oncological outcomes (RECIST, ECOG, tumor staging, overall survival, treatment response) and detailed clinical/demographic metadata (HLA, pregnancy, menopause, birth weight, etc.) which are not relevant to this microbiome research study.

The study does include disease-associated cohorts (colorectal cancer, type 2 diabetes, IBD, etc.) but only as meta-analysis comparisons of published datasets, not primary phenotypic data for individual participants.

All schema fields returned 'not_reported' because this paper reports microbial genomic diversity, population structure, and functional capacity but does not collect or report the clinical/phenotypic data covered by this schema.
Batch 2 returned granularity='study_level', differs from batch 0 ('sample_level'); kept batch 0.
Study is primarily a bacterial population genomics and metagenomics analysis, not a clinical trial or disease intervention study. No tumor measurements or intervention outcomes expected.
Schema fields 'tumor_size_residual_measurement' and 'antibiotics_exclusion_period' are inapplicable to this microbiome study design.
Target condition defined broadly as P. copri diversity/prevalence rather than specific disease phenotypes, though secondary disease associations were analyzed.
